expected_what.value: Quarterly, the reviewer pulls a report of everyone with admin-level access across core systems and confirms line-by-line whether each person still needs that access, signing off on the review.

expected_who.value: R. Fischer, Senior Systems Administrator, performs the review. The same individual is also the one who grants admin access whenever it is requested during the quarter.

expected_when.value: Last week of every quarter, as a recurring calendar task.

expected_why.value: To catch admin rights left over from a role someone has since moved out of, or a temporary access grant that was never removed.

expected_where.value: The reviewed spreadsheet, with sign-off date, is saved to a shared drive folder called "Access Reviews."

expected_how.value: Current job title is checked against a list of roles that justify admin access; the person's manager is asked to confirm where the reviewer is unsure.

source.excerpt: I pull a report of everyone with admin-level access across our core systems
I'm also the one who grants admin access whenever someone requests it during the quarter
make sure nobody's still got admin rights from a role they've since moved out of
I save the reviewed spreadsheet with my sign-off date in a shared drive folder
I check their current job title against a list of roles that justify admin access

expected_design_rationale: All six attributes are fully documented, but the control objective specifically requires the review to be performed by someone independent of the privileged-access provisioning process. The walkthrough directly establishes that the same individual (R. Fischer) both grants admin access during the quarter and reviews it at quarter-end (L06-L08). That lack of independence is a design flaw, not a documentation gap - it exists regardless of how well everything else is recorded, and it is the central issue a reviewer would raise for this control.

expected_risk_objective_control_alignmen.rationale: The control objective explicitly requires review by someone independent of provisioning. The interviewee directly confirms (L06-L08) that they perform both roles, with no compensating independent reviewer identified. This is a self-review condition that undermines the control's ability to detect inappropriate access the reviewer themselves granted.

reviewer_notes: Deliberately the inverse of a 'looks complete = must be fine' trap: every attribute is answerable, but the alignment problem is buried in the answer to a single follow-up question (L05-L08). Tests whether AssureAI reads for substance (independence) rather than just checking that all six boxes have text in them, and whether it can cite evidence for a NEGATIVE conclusion, not only positive ones.
